about: Candidate role × action permission matrix derived from frozen v46 evidence (Phase-0 audit, read-only) — final edition after adversarial verification. Not policy: no permission matrix was designed (HANDOFF-AUDIT-v46 item 7).

statusDefinitions.CONFIRMED: Stated by BC / stakeholder record / LD-M / handoff rule / explicit board 'Rules' statement (BOARD-RULE) AND boards draw it consistently, with no open T-/OD-/REG- item governing that point and no stakeholder record contradicting that point.
statusDefinitions.PROVISIONAL: Drawn (control or designed absence) or designed safe treatment, but not stated as a rule, governed by an open T-/OD-/REG- item, or contradicted by a stakeholder record while v46 / a locked decision gives a designed treatment; basis INFERRED = not drawn anywhere and not needed by a workflow (never build).
statusDefinitions.UNRESOLVED: Needed by a workflow but not drawn, contradictory between boards / JSON / stakeholder records without a designed treatment, or explicitly open with no safe treatment.

kindDefinitions.ALLOW: The design offers the action to the role. The only kind that grants anything.
kindDefinitions.DENY: Explicitly not permitted / not offered (designed absence, rule, or inferred absence).
kindDefinitions.READ: Visibility of a record or state.
kindDefinitions.SYSTEM: A transition no human control performs; a typed mock-service event in the build.
kindDefinitions.OPEN: Undecided capability (not drawn or drawn inconsistently, no designed treatment). Always UNRESOLVED; never offered in the build (P4); Notes give the safe treatment.

principles.text: PUBLIC is a surface, not a role. Exactly seven authenticated roles: Student, Faculty, Institute Admin, Vendor, Academic Reviewer, Content Manager, Super Admin; no eighth role (Learner = Student; Tenant Admin = Institute Admin; internal content teams work as Vendor).

One role per signed-in person; role-based landing after sign-in. No generic DEMO banner, sample-account chooser or developer-only account selector in the product (owner constraint). No role switcher, ‘Viewing as…’ or ‘choose a workspace’ step while multi-role (XS-02) is deferred.
principles.evidence: Owner binding constraints; B1-09 dt ‘Never here’; 06 nav rules; XS-02 DEFER (REG-XS-02 WAIT FOR DECISION); BR-006
principles.status: CONFIRMED (no DEMO banner / sample-account or developer selector — SES-04) · PROVISIONAL (one role per person, no role switcher — REG-XS-02; ROLE-13, SES-10)

principles.text: Each workspace has one base route (proposals: /student, /faculty, /institute, /vendor, /reviewer, /content-manager, /admin). An address belonging to another workspace renders XS-06 “This page isn’t part of your workspace” (Back to Home · Help) — never route names, role codes or technical causes. Entitlement refusals inside the Student workspace (ST-19 family: not given · no longer given · paused · ended) are a different mechanism from XS-06.

principles.text: “Role guards per workspace; actions offered only where the design offers them (e.g. no Publish for the Super Admin, approve-only device transfers).” A control absent from the boards is not permitted. derived/controls-by-workspace.json is evidence of what each role is shown, not policy.

principles.text: 0 links from one role’s frame into another role’s workspace; cross-role movement only through the shared public request-status page and Help & support.

Browse published content; build a selection in the browser session; submit a request; open the request status page from the same session (reference ≠ key); continue to a provider-neutral payment page (external route); sign in. Never: buy / check out, register an account, gain any access. Not offered while open: prices (ND-08), self-classification as internal / external (T-04), a reply to an information request (T-03).

principles.text: Student: self only — experiments from own SACC (individual or group), formats inherited from the plan (LD-1); own RUN/FB/ATT/DTR/SUP. · Faculty: courses assigned in Faculty courses (FCM, set by the IA) ∩ experiments the institution holds (ACC); reach = students given the experiment (SACC); co-teaching Faculty see the course’s assessment (OD-B4-17, ASMT-13) — editing between co-teachers is UNRESOLVED (ASMT-17). · Institute Admin: own institution only; can grant only experiments in an active plan (STK31-24). · Vendor: own submissions (‘Every experiment you created’); course list from Super-Admin-assigned scope (PROVISIONAL: T-29 / OD-B5-01 — CRS-08, SUB-11) — person-held on B7-08 vs organisation wording on B5-03 (UNRESOLVED, ROLE-08). · Academic Reviewer: ROLE scope all / course / experiment set by the Super Admin (STK31-41); queue = scope (PROVISIONAL, OD-B6-01 — SUB-23). · Content Manager: ROLE scope (‘Decides publication and raises corrections for: …’, B7-08); drawn only with ‘All experiments’ (PROVISIONAL — ROLE-10); platform course codes are platform-wide (M-2). · Super Admin: platform-wide; never publishes; never grants Student access; read-only on published content (M-1) and on the platform course code (M-2) — both are the v46 position but PROVISIONAL, because stakeholder records 07.2-E / 07.2-F / STK31-08 / STK31-09 ask for more (EXP-07, CC-07; owner decides).
principles.status: CONFIRMED except where rows say otherwise (scope sources marked PROVISIONAL above)

principles.text: Published ≠ institution access (ACC) ≠ Student entitlement (SACC) ≠ runtime activity (RUN) ≠ learning completion. Publishing or releasing never writes ACC or SACC. Completed is set by the system (event open, T-12), never by the Student, never inferred from a launch. Progress is per format with no aggregate verdict.

Paused institution → IA pages read-only, no Give/Withdraw, Students can’t open experiments, device requests can’t be forwarded, its requests can’t be decided; Faculty: banner only (OD-B7-07). Inactive Student → nothing opens. Vendor course withdrawn → saved draft read-only. Submission under review → Vendor read-only. Published → read-only for Vendor, Reviewer, SA and in CM live view. Update with Reviewer/SA → CM only ‘Open update’. Confirmed marks → read-only.

principles.id: P11 · System transitions are mock services
principles.text: Runtime activity/completion, payment confirmation, expiry clock, result release by setting, resubmission routing and objective marking are system events served by typed mock services that return the sample world. Board controls (‘Restart’, ‘Sample: …’, ‘Move the sample date past the deadline’, ‘The workflow routes the resubmission’) are canvas-only and never product.
